findings.body: Every AssignmentSource instance shares the single datetime evaluated once when the class body executed at import time, so queued never reflects when the source was actually created; any timing/expiry logic based on queued is silently wrong.
findings.failure_mode: Runtime value silently incorrect; not caught because the test only asserts the field is not None.
findings.impact: Every AssignmentSource instance shares the single datetime evaluated once when the class body executed at import time, so queued never reflects when the source was actually created; any timing/expiry logic based on queued is silently wrong.
findings.root_cause: A dataclass field default is set to the call result timezone.now() which is evaluated a single time at class-definition time rather than per instantiation.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a per-instance default: `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)` (importing `field` from dataclasses).
findings.title: queued default timestamp is frozen at module import time
findings.trigger: Any code that constructs AssignmentSource (e.g. AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)) after the module has been imported and later inspects the queued field.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 18 shows `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` as a dataclass field default. This is evaluated once at class definition time, not per-instance. All instances will share the same frozen timestamp. This is a well-known Python dataclass pitfall and the patch clearly introduces it.

pr.body:
## The problem:
When a Jira issue's `assignee` field is quickly modified multiple times in a row, we end up assigning and resyncing the assignees to Jira, which causes a loop. This is because _all_ inbound integration webhooks that modify an issue assignment generate an outbound update for all issue sync integrations as well.

## Solution:
This PR adds a new `AssignmentSource` dataclass, which acts as a context carrier when an external webhook triggers an issue assignment change. This is then checked on the outbound sync logic, preventing the change from being propagated to the same integration that initially triggered the change.
pr.title: fix(ecosystem): Breaks issue sync cycles

raw_findings.body: Every AssignmentSource instance shares the single datetime evaluated once when the class body executed at import time, so queued never reflects when the source was actually created; any timing/expiry logic based on queued is silently wrong.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Runtime value silently incorrect; not caught because the test only asserts the field is not None.
raw_findings.impact: Every AssignmentSource instance shares the single datetime evaluated once when the class body executed at import time, so queued never reflects when the source was actually created; any timing/expiry logic based on queued is silently wrong.
raw_findings.root_cause: A dataclass field default is set to the call result timezone.now() which is evaluated a single time at class-definition time rather than per instantiation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use a per-instance default: `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)` (importing `field` from dataclasses).
raw_findings.title: queued default timestamp is frozen at module import time
raw_findings.trigger: Any code that constructs AssignmentSource (e.g. AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)) after the module has been imported and later inspects the queued field.

raw_findings.body: If the task serializer is JSON, enqueuing raises a serialization error for the datetime value, so the outbound assignee sync task is never queued and the cycle-break/sync silently fails.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Task enqueue may raise at runtime depending on serializer configuration.
raw_findings.impact: If the task serializer is JSON, enqueuing raises a serialization error for the datetime value, so the outbound assignee sync task is never queued and the cycle-break/sync silently fails.
raw_findings.root_cause: to_dict() forwards a raw datetime object into celery task kwargs without ensuring JSON-serializability.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Serialize queued to an ISO string in to_dict (or exclude it from the transmitted dict) so assignment_source_dict contains only JSON-serializable primitives.
raw_findings.title: to_dict emits a datetime that may not be serializable in task kwargs
raw_findings.trigger: An inbound webhook triggers assign/deassign, passing an AssignmentSource whose to_dict() includes the queued datetime; sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async then serializes this dict for the broker.

raw_findings.body: The abstract method advertises cycle-breaking support for status sync that is never wired through, misleading implementers and leaving dead API surface inconsistent with the assignee path.
raw_findings.impact: The abstract method advertises cycle-breaking support for status sync that is never wired through, misleading implementers and leaving dead API surface inconsistent with the assignee path.
raw_findings.root_cause: New parameter added to the abstract status-sync method without a corresponding caller providing it.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either thread assignment_source through the sync_status_outbound task call site and should_sync('outbound_status', ...), or drop the unused parameter from the abstract signature.
raw_findings.title: sync_status_outbound gains assignment_source param that is never populated
raw_findings.trigger: Reviewing/using the new sync_status_outbound signature; the only caller (sync_status_outbound task) never passes assignment_source.
